subject: Dedicated reservation options + activation triggers for Solstice Health
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@solsticehealth.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation options + activation triggers for Solstice Health

Hi Lina —

Great to meet yesterday. Per our call, attached is an initial cover of two reservation profiles tuned to Solstice's peak batch inference and daytime low-latency traffic patterns. High-level options are below; the attached PDF (Solstice_Reserved_Offer_v1.pdf) has pricing and SLA callouts.

Option A — Anchored Minimal: 24x GPUs reserved (min 12 active)
- GPU type: H100-80GB preferred (we can price A100 as an alternate)
- Ramp: 4-week warmup with 50% reserved billing week 1 then step to 100% in week 5
- Use case: predictable nightly batch windows + steady async embedding workloads
- Pricing: $X per GPU-hour reserved; demo credits applied for month 1

Option B — Elastic Lane: 12–48 GPU tranche with burst lanes and guaranteed min of 12
- GPU mix: H100 + A100 fallbacks for cost-sensitive bursts
- Ramp: anchor at 20 GPUs first 90 days, monthly step-downs allowed with 30-day notice
- Use case: ramping product usage with occasional peaks (recommended if you expect growth)

Activation triggers and safeguards we recommend:
- Canary week: run production traffic to 10% of requests routed to the dedicated cluster for validation
- Autoscaling windows & burst reservations for 2-hour planned spikes
- Fallback policy: auto-route to hosted fallback model (same family) if cluster unavailable

Next steps I propose: review options with procurement, choose preferred GPU type (H100 vs A100), and confirm target anchor for month 0–3 so we can provide a DocuSign-ready offer. If helpful, I can update the offer to show a 20->12 staged ramp (Option B variant).

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options + activation triggers for Solstice Health

Thanks Mateo — helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and infra: 

1) Which exact instance SKU are you modeling for the H100 pricing? We need both H100-80GB and A100-80GB line items for our finance review.
2) Can the Elastic Lane mix GPUs inside a single tranche so we can backfill with A100 during non-peak hours?
3) Regarding geo/failover: our primary traffic is in us-west; we need to confirm cross-region burst support and cold-warm failover if a zone has capacity issues.
4) Procurement asked whether you can deliver a single DocuSign envelope that includes the ramp schedule and activation milestones (so we can attach to PO).

Looping in procurement for budget windows. Karthik, can you confirm the SKU/price matrix?

-Lina
Lina Gomez
Head of Cloud Platform, Solstice Health
lina.gomez@solsticehealth.io | +1 (617) 555-0890

Lina — quick answers and a recommended path based on similar deals. Attachment: Activation-Worksheet-Solstice.xlsx (xlsx)

1) SKU: we model H100-80GB (g5dn.h100-80) and A100-80GB (g5dn.a100-80) equivalence in the PDF pricing table. I can provide a line-item breakdown in the updated offer.
2) Yes — Option B supports mixed-instance backfills. You can configure priority for H100 during 08:00–20:00 PST; bursts will use A100 where available to keep latency SLAs within target.
3) Geo/failover: cross-region bursting is supported but adds egress and replication overhead. For the immediate onramp we recommend single-region anchoring (us-west) with hot-standby in us-east for DR.
4) DocuSign: we can publish a single envelope combining the reserved commitment, ramp schedule and activation checklist.

Recommendation: go with Option B but anchor at 20 GPUs for months 0–3 to give you capacity headroom while we validate traffic patterns. After 90 days, step to 12 with 30 days notice. We will include a 7-day canary and a rollback/fallback playbook in the activation worksheet.

Proposed timeline
- Aug 5: updated offer (final pricing + SKU table)
- Aug 6: DocuSign envelope sent for signature
- Aug 20: provisioning & canary week
- Sep 1: full traffic cutover (if canary passes)

If that works for procurement I can update the spreadsheet with committed hours and expected burn.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

- Adds SKU line-items for H100-80GB and A100-80GB so procurement can compare TCO
